title: Introduction — Why Truth Matters
summary: The authors argue that truth is objective and essential for evaluating worldviews. Christianity rises or falls on factual claims, not personal preference.
embedding_text: Truth corresponds to reality. If truth exists, contradictory worldviews cannot all be correct. Christianity invites investigation because it is rooted in historical events and testable claims.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 1 — Can We Handle the Truth?
summary: The authors challenge relativism and argue that moral and logical truths are unavoidable. Even denials of truth rely on truth claims.
embedding_text: Relativism self‑destructs because the claim 'there is no truth' is itself a truth claim. Logical laws are universal and necessary. Moral intuitions point toward objective standards.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 2 — Why Should Anyone Believe Anything?
summary: People believe things for sociological, psychological, religious, and evidential reasons. Only evidence provides a reliable foundation.
embedding_text: Beliefs based on upbringing or emotion are unstable. Evidence-based belief leads to truth. Christianity is grounded in historical events that can be examined.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 3 — In the Beginning, There Was a Great SURGE
summary: The authors outline scientific evidence that the universe had a beginning, using the acronym SURGE to summarize key discoveries.
embedding_text: SURGE: Second Law of Thermodynamics, Universe Expansion, Radiation Afterglow, Great Galaxy Seeds, Einstein’s Theory of General Relativity. These point to a finite beginning requiring a cause beyond space, time, and matter.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 4 — Divine Design
summary: The authors argue that the universe is finely tuned for life, and this precision points to intentional design.
embedding_text: Physical constants such as gravity, cosmological constant, and nuclear forces are calibrated with extreme precision. Even slight variations would make life impossible. Fine‑tuning suggests a purposeful designer.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 5 — The First Life: Natural Law or Divine Awe?
summary: The authors argue that natural processes cannot account for the origin of life, particularly the information encoded in DNA.
embedding_text: Life requires complex specified information. DNA functions like a language system. Natural laws can rearrange matter but cannot generate information. Intelligence is the best explanation for biological information.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 6 — New Life Forms: From the Goo to You via the Zoo?
summary: The authors critique Darwinian evolution and argue that macroevolution lacks sufficient evidence.
embedding_text: Microevolution is observable, but macroevolution requires new genetic information that natural selection cannot produce. The fossil record shows sudden appearance rather than gradual transitions.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 7 — Mother Teresa vs. Hitler
summary: The authors argue that objective morality exists and cannot be grounded in atheistic naturalism.
embedding_text: Moral differences between kindness and cruelty are not mere preferences. Objective morality requires a transcendent moral lawgiver. Without God, moral judgments reduce to personal opinion.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Chapter 8 — Miracles: Signs of God or Gullibility?
summary: The authors defend the possibility of miracles and argue that objections to miracles assume atheism rather than prove it.
embedding_text: If God exists, miracles are possible. Natural laws describe regular patterns but do not prevent the Creator from acting. Historical evidence supports the resurrection as a credible miracle.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: The Cosmological Argument — The Universe Had a Beginning
summary: Everything that begins to exist has a cause, and scientific evidence shows the universe had a beginning.
embedding_text: The universe is not eternal. Big Bang cosmology, expansion, and thermodynamics point to a finite beginning. The cause must be spaceless, timeless, immaterial, powerful, and personal.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: The Teleological Argument — Fine-Tuning Points to a Designer
summary: The extreme precision of physical constants and biological complexity indicate intentional design.
embedding_text: Fine‑tuning of cosmic constants and the information content of DNA exceed what chance or natural processes can produce. Design is the best explanation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: The Moral Argument — Objective Morality Requires a Moral Lawgiver
summary: Universal moral truths cannot arise from matter, chance, or human opinion.
embedding_text: If objective morality exists, it must come from a transcendent source. Naturalism cannot ground human dignity, rights, or moral obligation. Theism provides a coherent foundation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: The Resurrection — The Central Claim of Christianity
summary: The authors argue that the resurrection is supported by early testimony, eyewitness accounts, and the transformation of the disciples.
embedding_text: The resurrection is grounded in historical data: early creeds, empty tomb reports, hostile witnesses, and the radical change in the disciples. Alternative explanations like hallucinations or conspiracy fail to explain the evidence. The resurrection best accounts for the rise of Christianity.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Is the New Testament Reliable?
summary: The authors argue that the New Testament documents are historically trustworthy based on manuscript evidence, early dating, and corroboration.
embedding_text: Thousands of manuscripts, early quotations, and archaeological confirmations support the New Testament's accuracy. The short time gap between events and written accounts reduces legendary development. Non-Christian sources confirm key details.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Miracles Are Impossible
summary: The authors respond that miracles are possible if God exists, and the evidence for God makes miracles reasonable.
embedding_text: A miracle is not a violation of natural law but an intervention by the Creator who established those laws. If the universe had a beginning and is designed, then the God who created it can act within it. The resurrection is a historically supported miracle.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Bible Is Full of Errors
summary: The authors argue that alleged contradictions in the Bible often stem from misunderstandings of context, genre, or translation.
embedding_text: Most alleged contradictions dissolve when considering cultural context, literary style, or harmonization principles. Minor variations in eyewitness accounts actually support authenticity, as fabricated stories tend to be uniform.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Disciples Invented the Resurrection
summary: The authors argue that the disciples had no motive to invent the resurrection and suffered greatly for their testimony.
embedding_text: Liars make poor martyrs. The disciples gained no wealth, power, or comfort from preaching the resurrection. Their willingness to suffer and die indicates sincerity. Fabricating a resurrection would not explain the empty tomb or hostile witnesses.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Resurrection Was a Hallucination
summary: The authors argue that hallucinations are individual experiences and cannot explain group appearances or the empty tomb.
embedding_text: Hallucinations do not occur in groups, nor do they produce physical evidence like an empty tomb. The variety of resurrection appearances—indoors, outdoors, to individuals and groups—contradicts the hallucination hypothesis.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Resurrection Was a Legend
summary: The authors argue that the resurrection accounts are too early and too detailed to be legendary.
embedding_text: Legends require long periods to develop, but the resurrection proclamation began immediately after the events. Early creeds like 1 Corinthians 15 date to within a few years of the crucifixion, leaving no time for myth-making.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Copied Pagan Myths
summary: The authors argue that alleged parallels between Christianity and pagan myths are exaggerated or fabricated.
embedding_text: Claims that Christianity borrowed from pagan myths ignore historical timelines and distort pagan stories. Most supposed parallels were written after Christianity or lack meaningful similarity. The resurrection stands on historical evidence, not mythological borrowing.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Science Eliminates the Need for God
summary: The authors argue that science explains natural processes but cannot explain the origin of nature itself.
embedding_text: Science describes how the universe behaves, not why it exists. Scientific laws require a lawgiver. The origin of the universe, fine‑tuning, and moral law point beyond natural processes to a transcendent cause.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Evolution Explains Everything
summary: The authors argue that evolution cannot explain the origin of life, consciousness, morality, or the fine‑tuning of the universe.
embedding_text: Even if evolution explains biological diversity, it does not explain the origin of life, the information in DNA, or the existence of consciousness. Evolution presupposes a functioning universe and biological system, which require explanation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Universe Created Itself
summary: The authors argue that self‑creation is logically impossible because something cannot exist before it exists.
embedding_text: Self‑creation violates the law of non‑contradiction. The universe cannot bring itself into existence because it would need to exist before it existed. A cause outside the universe is required.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Universe Is Eternal
summary: The authors argue that scientific evidence overwhelmingly supports a finite beginning to the universe.
embedding_text: The second law of thermodynamics, cosmic expansion, and background radiation all indicate a universe with a beginning. An eternal universe is incompatible with modern cosmology.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Resurrection Was a Conspiracy
summary: The authors argue that conspiracies require power, secrecy, and consistency—none of which fit the disciples’ situation.
embedding_text: Conspiracies collapse under pressure, but the disciples maintained their testimony under persecution. They lacked political power, had no motive to lie, and faced severe consequences. A conspiracy cannot explain the empty tomb or post‑resurrection appearances.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Disciples Stole the Body
summary: The authors argue that the disciples lacked motive, opportunity, and courage to steal Jesus’ body.
embedding_text: Roman guards faced execution for failure, making theft unlikely. The disciples were fearful and in hiding before the resurrection. Stealing the body would not explain post‑resurrection appearances or their later boldness.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Women Went to the Wrong Tomb
summary: The authors argue that the wrong‑tomb theory fails because both Jewish and Roman authorities knew the correct location.
embedding_text: If the women went to the wrong tomb, authorities could have easily corrected the mistake by producing the body. The tomb belonged to a known figure, Joseph of Arimathea, making confusion unlikely.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Jesus Only Fainted
summary: The authors argue that the swoon theory is medically impossible given Roman execution methods.
embedding_text: Roman crucifixion ensured death through scourging, blood loss, and asphyxiation. A half‑dead Jesus could not move the stone, overpower guards, and inspire belief in a victorious resurrection.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Resurrection Was a Spiritual Vision
summary: The authors argue that Jewish beliefs about resurrection involved physical bodies, not spiritual visions.
embedding_text: First‑century Jews expected bodily resurrection at the end of time, not spiritual visions. The empty tomb and physical interactions with Jesus contradict a purely spiritual interpretation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospels Were Written Too Late
summary: The authors argue that the Gospels were written early enough to be based on eyewitness testimony.
embedding_text: Acts ends before Paul’s death (AD 64–67), implying Luke was written earlier. Luke used Mark, placing Mark even earlier. Early creeds and quotations show that core Christian beliefs existed within years of the events.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospels Are Biased
summary: The authors argue that bias does not invalidate testimony, especially when the writers had nothing to gain.
embedding_text: The Gospel writers gained persecution, not power. Bias must be demonstrated, not assumed. Their willingness to suffer supports sincerity, and hostile sources confirm many details.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospels Are Anonymous
summary: The authors argue that early church tradition consistently attributes the Gospels to their traditional authors.
embedding_text: Anonymous documents were common in antiquity. Early Christian writers unanimously identify Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John as the authors. No competing authorship traditions exist.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospels Are Full of Legendary Embellishment
summary: The authors argue that the Gospels contain realistic, counterproductive, and culturally awkward details that legends avoid.
embedding_text: Women as first witnesses, slow‑to‑believe disciples, and embarrassing failures are unlikely inventions. The Gospels lack the exaggerated style typical of later legends.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Disciples Were Fooled by Someone Who Looked Like Jesus
summary: The authors argue that mistaken identity cannot explain the variety and nature of resurrection appearances.
embedding_text: Jesus appeared multiple times, in different locations, to individuals and groups. Mistaken identity cannot explain physical interactions, extended conversations, or the empty tomb.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Resurrection Was a Later Invention
summary: The authors argue that the resurrection was proclaimed immediately, not developed over time.
embedding_text: Early creeds like 1 Corinthians 15 date to within a few years of the crucifixion. The earliest Christians centered their message on the resurrection from the beginning.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Worldview Comparison: Theism vs. Atheism
summary: The authors compare the explanatory power of theism and atheism regarding origins, morality, consciousness, and meaning.
embedding_text: Theism explains the universe’s beginning, fine‑tuning, moral law, and human consciousness. Atheism struggles to account for these features without invoking chance or uncaused processes.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Worldview Comparison: Naturalism vs. Christianity
summary: The authors argue that naturalism cannot explain immaterial realities such as logic, morality, and consciousness.
embedding_text: If only matter exists, then thoughts, moral obligations, and rationality become illusions. Christianity provides a coherent foundation for immaterial truths and human dignity.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Worldview Comparison: Pantheism vs. Christianity
summary: The authors argue that pantheism collapses distinctions between good and evil and denies the reality of the physical world.
embedding_text: Pantheism claims everything is divine, making moral distinctions meaningless. Christianity affirms a real world created by a personal God, grounding morality and purpose.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Worldview Comparison: Postmodernism vs. Truth
summary: The authors argue that postmodernism undermines itself by denying objective truth while relying on truth claims.
embedding_text: Postmodernism asserts that truth is socially constructed, yet this claim itself is presented as objectively true. The view collapses under its own logic. Objective truth is necessary for meaningful communication.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Worldview Comparison: Agnosticism vs. Knowledge
summary: The authors argue that agnosticism is often a temporary position because evidence can be evaluated.
embedding_text: Agnosticism claims that knowledge of God is impossible, yet this is itself a knowledge claim. Evidence from cosmology, morality, and history provides grounds for belief.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: We Cannot Trust Eyewitness Testimony
summary: The authors argue that eyewitness testimony is foundational to historical investigation and is reliable when multiple independent sources agree.
embedding_text: Eyewitness testimony is the backbone of historical knowledge. Independent accounts, early reporting, and corroboration strengthen reliability. The New Testament contains multiple eyewitness perspectives that align on core events.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Disciples Were Illiterate and Could Not Write
summary: The authors argue that literacy in the ancient world was more widespread than often assumed, especially among Jewish communities.
embedding_text: First‑century Jews valued education, and many could read or write at basic levels. Even if some disciples were not highly literate, they could use scribes. The argument from illiteracy does not undermine Gospel authorship.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospels Were Edited Over Time
summary: The authors argue that manuscript evidence shows remarkable stability in the Gospel texts.
embedding_text: Thousands of manuscripts allow scholars to identify and correct copying errors. Variants rarely affect meaning. The core message of the Gospels has remained consistent across centuries.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Gospel Writers Invented Prophecy Fulfillment
summary: The authors argue that many prophecies fulfilled by Jesus were outside His human control.
embedding_text: Events such as birthplace, method of death, and burial location were not self‑engineered. The convergence of multiple independent prophecies strengthens the case for divine orchestration.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Bible Was Changed at the Council of Nicaea
summary: The authors argue that Nicaea addressed Christological disputes, not the biblical canon.
embedding_text: The Council of Nicaea did not rewrite Scripture. It affirmed doctrines already held by the early church. Manuscripts predating Nicaea confirm that the biblical text remained consistent.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Just One Religion Among Many
summary: The authors argue that Christianity is unique because it is rooted in historical events, not merely moral teachings.
embedding_text: Most religions emphasize ethical systems or philosophical ideas. Christianity centers on a historical claim: the resurrection. If the resurrection occurred, Christianity is uniquely validated.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Religious Belief Is Just Wishful Thinking
summary: The authors argue that wishful thinking cannot explain the hardships early Christians endured.
embedding_text: People do not willingly suffer persecution for comforting fantasies. The early Christians proclaimed the resurrection despite severe consequences, indicating conviction based on evidence, not wishful thinking.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Faith and Reason Are Opposites
summary: The authors argue that biblical faith is trust based on evidence, not blind belief.
embedding_text: Faith in Scripture means relying on what one has good reason to believe is true. Christianity encourages investigation and appeals to historical and philosophical evidence.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: You Cannot Prove God Exists
summary: The authors argue that while absolute proof is rare in any field, strong evidence can justify belief in God.
embedding_text: Most important truths—scientific, historical, or personal—are accepted based on evidence, not mathematical certainty. Cosmology, morality, and design provide cumulative evidence for God.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Belief in God Is a Psychological Crutch
summary: The authors argue that psychological motives do not determine truth.
embedding_text: Even if some people believe in God for comfort, this does not address whether God exists. Motives cannot replace evidence. Atheism can also function as a psychological crutch to avoid moral accountability.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Religion Causes Violence
summary: The authors argue that human evil, not religion itself, causes violence, and atheistic regimes have committed atrocities on a massive scale.
embedding_text: Violence arises from human nature, not belief systems alone. Secular ideologies like communism have produced more deaths than religious conflicts. Christianity condemns violence and teaches love of neighbor.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: God Should Reveal Himself More Clearly
summary: The authors argue that God provides sufficient evidence for seekers while allowing freedom for those who resist.
embedding_text: God balances clarity with human freedom. Evidence exists in creation, conscience, Scripture, and the resurrection. Demanding overwhelming proof would undermine free will and genuine relationship.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: If God Exists, Why Is There Evil?
summary: The authors argue that the existence of evil actually supports the existence of God because evil presupposes an objective moral standard.
embedding_text: Calling something evil assumes a standard of goodness. Without God, moral categories collapse into personal preference. The problem of evil is a challenge for all worldviews, but Christianity offers both explanation and hope.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: A Good God Would Not Allow Suffering
summary: The authors argue that suffering can serve greater purposes, including moral growth, free will, and the possibility of love.
embedding_text: A world without suffering would eliminate courage, compassion, and meaningful choice. God can use suffering to accomplish long‑term good. The cross shows that God enters human suffering rather than avoiding it.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Hell Is Immoral
summary: The authors argue that hell respects human freedom and reflects the seriousness of rejecting God.
embedding_text: Hell is not arbitrary punishment but the natural consequence of choosing separation from God. Love requires freedom, and freedom includes the possibility of rejecting God eternally.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: God Is Hidden
summary: The authors argue that God provides enough evidence for seekers while allowing freedom for those who resist.
embedding_text: God reveals Himself through creation, conscience, Scripture, and the resurrection. Hiddenness preserves human freedom and prevents coerced belief. Evidence is sufficient but not overwhelming, allowing genuine relationship rather than forced acknowledgment.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Religion Is a Product of Culture
summary: The authors argue that cultural influence does not determine truth.
embedding_text: People often adopt beliefs from their environment, but this does not make those beliefs false. Truth is independent of cultural background. Evidence, not geography, determines whether Christianity is true.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christians Are Hypocrites
summary: The authors argue that moral failure among Christians does not invalidate Christianity’s truth claims.
embedding_text: Hypocrisy contradicts Christian teaching but does not disprove the resurrection or the existence of God. The validity of a worldview depends on evidence, not the behavior of its followers.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Too Exclusive
summary: The authors argue that truth by nature is exclusive, and Christianity’s claims must be evaluated on their merits.
embedding_text: All truth claims exclude their opposites. Christianity is not unique in being exclusive; every worldview makes exclusive claims. The question is which worldview is true based on evidence.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Science
summary: The authors argue that Christianity historically fostered scientific discovery and is compatible with scientific investigation.
embedding_text: Many founders of modern science were Christians who believed the universe was orderly because it was created by a rational God. Christianity explains why science works: the universe is intelligible and governed by consistent laws.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Miracles Violate Natural Law
summary: The authors argue that miracles do not violate natural law but represent God’s intervention in His creation.
embedding_text: Natural laws describe regular patterns; they do not prevent God from acting. A miracle is not a contradiction of nature but an addition of supernatural power. The resurrection fits this category.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Universe Does Not Need a Designer
summary: The authors argue that the fine‑tuning of the universe strongly suggests intentional design.
embedding_text: The precise calibration of physical constants cannot be explained by chance or necessity. The universe appears engineered for life. Design is the most reasonable explanation for fine‑tuning.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Morality Is Just a Human Invention
summary: The authors argue that objective morality cannot arise from human opinion or evolutionary processes.
embedding_text: If morality is subjective, no action can be universally condemned. Evolutionary explanations reduce morality to survival instincts, not objective duties. The existence of real moral obligations points to a transcendent moral lawgiver.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Consciousness Can Be Explained Materially
summary: The authors argue that consciousness cannot be reduced to physical processes.
embedding_text: Thoughts, intentions, and self‑awareness are immaterial realities. Materialism cannot explain subjective experience or rationality. Consciousness points to a non‑material source consistent with theism.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Free Will Is an Illusion
summary: The authors argue that free will is necessary for rationality, morality, and responsibility.
embedding_text: If all thoughts are determined by physical processes, then reasoning collapses. Free will is required for moral accountability and meaningful choice. Theism provides a foundation for genuine freedom.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Universe Could Be a Multiverse
summary: The authors argue that the multiverse hypothesis does not eliminate the need for a designer.
embedding_text: A multiverse would still require fine‑tuned mechanisms to generate universes. It shifts the problem rather than solving it. The multiverse itself would need explanation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: The Bible Is Mythology
summary: The authors argue that the Bible differs from mythology in genre, historical detail, and eyewitness grounding.
embedding_text: Myths use symbolic language and lack historical anchors. The Bible includes names, dates, locations, and verifiable events. Archaeology repeatedly confirms biblical details.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Suppresses Human Freedom
summary: The authors argue that Christianity enhances freedom by grounding human dignity and moral responsibility.
embedding_text: Freedom requires objective moral boundaries. Christianity affirms human worth and provides a framework for meaningful choice. Moral relativism ultimately undermines freedom.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Intellectual
summary: The authors argue that Christianity encourages the pursuit of truth and has historically supported education and scholarship.
embedding_text: Christian thinkers have shaped philosophy, science, and literature. The biblical worldview affirms reason as a gift from God. Christianity invites rigorous investigation.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Based on Blind Faith
summary: The authors argue that Christianity is grounded in evidence, not blind belief.
embedding_text: Biblical faith is trust in what one has good reason to believe is true. The resurrection, fulfilled prophecy, and historical reliability of Scripture provide a rational foundation for Christian faith.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Just Emotional Comfort
summary: The authors argue that Christianity often brings hardship rather than comfort, showing that belief is grounded in conviction, not emotion.
embedding_text: Early Christians faced persecution, loss of status, and death. Emotional comfort cannot explain their willingness to suffer. Christianity’s truth claims stand independently of emotional appeal.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Based on Ignorance
summary: The authors argue that Christianity is rooted in historical events and rational investigation, not ignorance.
embedding_text: Christianity encourages the use of reason and evidence. The resurrection, fulfilled prophecy, and manuscript reliability provide intellectual grounding. Ignorance cannot account for Christianity’s historical impact.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Oppressive
summary: The authors argue that Christianity historically elevated human dignity, inspired charity, and advanced human rights.
embedding_text: Christian teaching affirms the equal worth of all people. Christian movements have driven abolition, education, and humanitarian work. Oppression contradicts Christian ethics rather than flowing from them.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Reason
summary: The authors argue that Christianity is compatible with rational inquiry and has shaped Western intellectual tradition.
embedding_text: Christian thinkers like Augustine, Aquinas, and Pascal integrated faith with reason. The biblical worldview affirms that humans are rational beings created by a rational God.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Freedom
summary: The authors argue that Christianity supports genuine freedom by grounding moral responsibility and human dignity.
embedding_text: Freedom requires moral boundaries and intrinsic human worth. Christianity affirms both. Moral relativism undermines freedom by removing objective standards.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Sex
summary: The authors argue that Christianity affirms sexuality within a moral framework designed for human flourishing.
embedding_text: Christian sexual ethics emphasize commitment, fidelity, and mutual respect. Boundaries protect individuals and relationships. Christianity is not anti‑sex but pro‑healthy sexuality.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Pleasure
summary: The authors argue that Christianity affirms pleasure within proper boundaries and warns against destructive excess.
embedding_text: Pleasure is a gift from God but becomes harmful when detached from moral order. Christianity promotes long‑term joy over short‑term indulgence.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Progress
summary: The authors argue that Christianity historically fueled scientific, moral, and social progress.
embedding_text: Christian belief in a rational Creator inspired scientific exploration. Christian ethics shaped human rights, charity, and education. Progress aligns with Christian principles.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Objection: Christianity Is Anti‑Diversity
summary: The authors argue that Christianity is a global faith that transcends ethnicity, culture, and geography.
embedding_text: Christianity spread across diverse cultures without erasing identity. Its core message applies universally because it addresses universal human needs.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Reality of Sin
summary: The authors argue that human moral failure is universal and confirms the biblical view of sin.
embedding_text: Human beings consistently fall short of moral ideals. This universal pattern aligns with the Christian doctrine of sin, which explains both human greatness and human corruption.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Desire for Meaning
summary: The authors argue that humans naturally seek purpose, which points beyond material existence.
embedding_text: Meaning cannot be grounded in a purely material universe. The human longing for purpose suggests we are made for more than survival. Christianity provides a coherent framework for meaning.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Longing for Justice
summary: The authors argue that the universal desire for justice points to a moral standard beyond human society.
embedding_text: People instinctively recognize injustice and desire accountability. This longing implies an objective moral order. Christianity explains justice through God’s character and final judgment.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Search for Identity
summary: The authors argue that human identity cannot be grounded solely in material or social categories.
embedding_text: Identity rooted in achievements or social roles is unstable. Christianity grounds identity in being created and loved by God, providing stability and dignity.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Experience of Guilt
summary: The authors argue that guilt reflects real moral responsibility, not merely social conditioning.
embedding_text: Guilt arises when we violate moral law. Its universality suggests an objective moral standard. Christianity offers both explanation and redemption for guilt.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Desire for Love
summary: The authors argue that the human longing for unconditional love points to a transcendent source.
embedding_text: Love is more than a chemical reaction; it reflects deep relational design. Christianity teaches that humans are made in the image of a relational God, explaining our desire for love.
source: I Don't Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist

title: Human Nature: The Longing for Transcendence
summary: The authors argue that humans naturally seek something beyond the material world, suggesting we are made for more than physical existence.
embedding_text: Across cultures, humans express spiritual longing through worship, art, and philosophy. This universal desire points to a transcendent source. Christianity explains this longing as evidence that humans are created for relationship with God.
